text:
Rae: Quick thread 1 1 legend contrast + keyboard affordance on the metrics dashboard. Support reported low contrast on inactive legend items; keyboard users also can't tell which series is focused. Need proposals.

Tom: Saw it. In dense charts the legend uses muted labels with 50% opacity; that fails contrast for small text. Suggest we use a token for 'muted-on-surface' that meets 4.5:1 for 12px text, or increase font weight for small sizes.

Aisha: From accessibility: contrast is critical. Also add a visible focus ring around the legend item when tabbed (not just outline:none). Use a high-contrast ring and preserve the color indicator square.

Ivy: UX thought: when a legend item is keyboard-focused, we could temporarily bold the label, increase contrast, and add a dashed focus inset around the color chip. Avoid moving layout.

Rae: Microcopy question: should the focus state include an affordance like "(press Enter to highlight)"? For SR, maybe the legend item role should be button and have `aria-pressed` to indicate highlighted state.

Aisha: Yes — role="button" and `aria-pressed="true|false"`. Also announce changes via `aria-live="polite"`: e.g., "Series A focused. Press Enter to isolate series." Keep short.

Tom: CSS sketch for focus ring & chip:
```css
.legend-item { display:flex; gap:8px; align-items:center; }
.legend-item__chip { width:12px; height:12px; border-radius:2px; }
.legend-item:focus { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--focus); }
.legend-item--muted { color: var(--muted-on-surface); }
```

Ivy: Important: do not rely only on color to convey state. Add an icon for hidden/disabled series (eye/eye-off), and a text-only suffix for small screens (e.g., "(hidden)").

Rae: Also thinking about colorblind-friendly palettes for chips. Use patterns or subtle textures? Might add an alternating stroke pattern for up to 6 series. But we should keep visuals simple. Perhaps a secondary shape (circle vs square) when two series have confusing hues.

Aisha: For SR: announce both label and color descriptor: "Latency, color blue" is ok, but color alone is not sufficient. Better: "Latency, series 1 (blue, solid)" if we add shape or stroke. Keep aria-label consistent: `aria-label="Latency series, highlighted"` when pressed.

Tom: Interaction edge-case: keyboard users tabbing through many legend items can be tedious. Propose arrow-key navigation within the legend (roving tabindex) so only one item is tabbable. Left/right up/down to move. That keeps tab order short.

Ivy: Good call. If we do roving tabindex, ensure screen reader users still get proper announcements when focused changes; update aria-live accordingly. Also ensure mobile still supports touch tap to toggle.

Rae: Copy options for the small SR hint when toggling isolate mode:
- "Isolating series. Press Enter again to show all."
- "Series isolated. Press Enter to return."
- "Series highlighted. Press Space to toggle isolation."
Which is best? I prefer second for clarity.

Aisha: I vote for clear verb + state: "Series isolated. Press Enter to return." Keep verb Enter consistent in docs. Also add a short tooltip for sighted users: "Press Enter to isolate this series" on hover/focus. Tooltip must be accessible with `aria-describedby`.

Tom: Tests: 1) visual regression for focused legend item (contrast tokens); 2) keyboard tests for roving tabindex; 3) aria-live snapshot with message when isolation toggles. I'll add those to legend.test.tsx.

Ivy: Implementation note: when isolated, other series should have `aria-hidden="true"` set visually but not removed from the DOM to avoid focus loss. Also add a small banner when isolated: "Viewing Latency only 1 Show all" so users know they're in a filtered view. Banner must be keyboard-focusable.

Rae: Action items: Tom 1 update CSS token and tests; Ivy 1 prototype roving tabindex + iconography; Aisha 1 write aria-live strings and tooltip patterns; Rae 1 finalize copy and design token names.

Tom: I'll open a draft PR with the CSS change and initial tests by EOD. :thumbsup:
